request.tone: wonder-filled island survey against the clock; violence none, scariness moderate, peril moderate
request.note: catalog book; plan extracted blind by reading the book

pitch.hero: Wren, a would-be Chart House apprentice left alone on an unnamed island with one blank sheet
pitch.want: to draw a true chart of the whole island before the ship returns at dusk and win the apprenticeship
pitch.obstacle: fast tides, mud, flooding caves, crumbling heights, and wonders that eat the day
pitch.stake: the apprenticeship, and the chart a lost mapmaker named Alder left half done
pitch.ending_kind: a finished named chart, a rescue, a partial chart, a discovery kept instead, or a setback

wren.name: Wren
wren.want: to chart the island true by dusk and earn the apprenticeship
wren.voice: close third past; curious, careful, tested on patience versus haste and wonder versus the clock

mate.name: the mate
mate.want: a true chart seen with the candidate's own eyes
mate.voice: weathered and terse; verdicts in short sayings

alder.name: Alder
alder.role: lost mapmaker, present only through marks, notes, letters and a half chart
alder.want: that whoever comes after finish the chart and give the island its name
alder.voice: a small sure hand; warm, plain, hopeful

sailors.name: two sailors
sailors.role: ship's crew sent ashore to the cove
sailors.want: to help with the rescue before the tide

truth.question: What waits on the unnamed island, and how can Wren finish a true chart of it before dusk?
truth.statement: The island was marked long ago by its first people and later by Alder, a mapmaker who left a family ashore, began a true chart, and carried it up to the ridge camp before a great storm. Alder never returned. The half chart waits at the camp with pens, a spyglass and a signal mirror, and Alder's wish that whoever finds it finish the chart and name the island. Only the summit above the camp shows the whole island at once, the one place to finish the chart before the ship returns at dusk.

wren_on_island.text: Wren is rowed ashore alone at first light onto an island no map has ever named.

wren_kit.text: Wren carries a satchel, a flask, and one blank sheet of paper.

the_mate.text: The mate of the ship brought Wren ashore and set the test.

chart_test.text: The test: fill the paper with a true chart of the island before the ship returns at dusk, or the apprenticeship goes to someone else.

ship_returns_dusk.text: The ship will come back for Wren at dusk.

chart_house.text: The Chart House is the mapmakers' house whose teaching, rules and keepers Wren knows and whose apprenticeship is at stake.

five_ways.text: Five ways lead inland from the beach: a mangrove coast, a cloud-forest ridge, sink-hole caverns, a ruined survey tower on the headland, and tidal flats.

first_people.text: People found and marked the island long before any mapmaker came.

alder_name.text: Someone named Alder left marks and writing on the island.

alder_mapmaker.text: Alder was a mapmaker who came to the island before Wren and wanted to be followed.

ridge_camp.text: There is a camp high on the island's ridge.

alder_chart_at_camp.text: Alder left a chart of the island at the ridge camp for whoever came after.

alder_storm.text: Alder carried the chart up to the ridge camp before a great storm, meaning to come back for it.

alder_never_returned.text: Alder never came home; the storm ended Alder's return.

camp_is_alders.text: A board above the camp's doorway is painted with the name Alder; it is Alder's camp.

cairn_line.text: A line of small cairns set by a careful hand marks the safe way up through the rubble and along the ridge to the camp.

mg_features.text: On the mangrove coast lie a fallen-log bridge upcoast, oyster rocks downcoast, a hidden creek inland, and a still green lagoon.

hidden_creek.text: A hidden creek runs inland from the mangrove coast under a roof of leaves.

log_bridge.text: A slippery fallen log crosses a channel upcoast while the tide turns beneath it.

carved_driftwood.text: A knot of driftwood wedged against the log bears old deliberate carved marks.

rookery_far_bank.text: A heron rookery clatters on the far bank of the log channel.

driftwood_arrows.text: The driftwood marks are mapmaker's shorthand with a compass rose; one arrow points to sea caves along the shore, the other up to high ground.

farbank_fork.text: Past the log the path splits: a quick risky mud slick to the left, firm palms to the right.

out_tide_cut_coast.text: Wren sank in the mud slick; the tide closed over the log bridge and cut off that corner of coast, left blank on the paper.

northern_view.text: From the high ground Wren sees the northern shape of the island and a long curl of reef offshore.

hidden_cove.text: A hidden cove of calm water is tucked into the island's cliffs inside the reef.

oyster_turtle.text: A small sea turtle lies stranded on its back in a draining pool among the oyster rocks, unhurt.

signal_plan.text: From a high place Wren could signal the ship so grown hands come before dusk to help a stranded animal.

out_turtle_righted.text: Wren righted the oyster-rock turtle and it swam free, but only the reef corner got mapped.

seep_from_spring.text: A clear sweet seep runs through the marsh, fed by a spring on higher ground.

flask_filled.text: Wren fills the flask with cold fresh water.

seep_fork.text: The fern gully forks toward a bright spring pool and a mossy overhang.

overhang_firepit.text: Under the mossy overhang lie an old firepit and a dented tin cup where someone sheltered before.

out_cozy_shelter.text: Wren sketched only the dry shelter while the morning slipped away.

otters.text: A mother otter and two kits live along the hidden creek.

heron_island.text: A loud heron island crowds the channel across the creek.

creek_sweet.text: Upstream the creek runs sweet, not salt, fed from higher on the island.

trees_brightness.text: Among the trees a brightness uphill promises open ground, while a level game trail runs flat and easy.

game_trail_loop.text: The game trail curls back on itself; it may be a loop that goes nowhere.

out_mangrove_maze.text: The game trail led Wren in a circle; the coast was guessed and its middle left blank.

lagoon_features.text: At the lagoon lie a half-sunk dugout canoe, a tunnel of arching roots, and a driftwood dam.

dugout_sound.text: The dugout is old but sound, carved from a single log.

out_sunk_canoe.text: The dugout sank under Wren far from shore; only the sketchbook stayed dry and the morning was lost.

cleared_ground.text: Across the lagoon lies a strip of old cleared ground with a stone mound and weathered posts.

fishing_camp.text: The mound and posts are the remains of a long-abandoned fishing camp of people who once lived on the island.

out_lost_village.text: Wren mapped the vanished village stone by stone instead of the coast.

root_tunnel_fork.text: The root tunnel forks: one way brightens toward open sky, the other bores deeper into the dark.

out_root_maze.text: Wren got lost in the branching root tunnels and backtracked by feel, leaving them a scribble.

alder_stake.text: A survey stake with a faded number and Alder's name stands in the otters' driftwood dam.

wren_has_stake.text: Wren prised Alder's survey stake free and carries it as a keepsake.

out_survey_stake.text: Wren carried the stake home like treasure and the map was hardly started.

heron_island_features.text: The heron island has a weathered watching blind on stilts, a wide mud bank, and a rookery in the treetops.

wren_has_raft.text: Wren lashed a reed raft to pole across to the heron island.

alder_blind.text: The watching blind was Alder's; its rails carry a carved tide table and compass bearings of every headland.

out_tide_table.text: Wren copied Alder's whole tide table and left the island's shape for another day.

firm_ribbon.text: A firm ribbon of packed sand crosses the soft mud bank toward a far channel.

out_bird_storm.text: Wren startled the flock, sank knee-deep, and the heron island went down as a smudge.

fallen_chick.text: A fallen heron chick lay in the rookery grass and Wren set it back on a branch.

out_rookery_watch.text: Wren watched and drew the heron colony while the coast went unmapped.

cf_ways.text: On the cloud-forest slope a steep switchback, a gentle traverse, a mossy hollow with a pale gleam, and a waterfall's roar offer ways up.

pale_gleam.text: Something pale gleams in a mossy hollow on the ridge slope.

switch_fork.text: On the switchback a bare rock rib climbs straight up and a green shelf curves to the side.

contour_path.text: The green shelf is a contour path a surveyor cut on purpose long ago.

grassy_bench.text: A broad grassy bench on the ridge's shoulder is where the ridge path toward the camp begins.

ancient_grove.text: A grove of giant mossy ancient trees stands off the ridge bench.

crest_fork.text: The ridge splits: the cairns follow a sheltered ledge below the crest, a bolder line runs over the airy crest.

out_ridge_vertigo.text: Wren froze on the airy ridge, edged back, and left the high camp unreached.

island_spring.text: The island has a spring: a cold clear pool ringed with ferns where its streams begin.

deer_path_dell.text: A narrow deer path leads aside to a hidden dell.

orchid_box.text: The pale gleam is a curtain of white orchids hiding a dry cleft with a mossy tin box marked with a compass rose.

box_contents.text: The tin box holds field notes, a pencil stub, and a dark brass locket.

locket_girl.text: The locket holds a faded picture of a young half-smiling girl who looks a little like Wren.

out_locket.text: Wren carried the locket's mystery home and the ridge was mapped in a distracted scrawl.

caverns_flood.text: Alder's notes warn that the caverns below flood fast and deep at high tide.

waterfall.text: A waterfall pours into a green pool, with a wet rock scramble beside it, a mossy log above the lip, and pale shapes in the pool.

out_falls_slip.text: Wren slipped on the wet rocks into the pool; the high ridge stayed unmapped.

alder_gauge.text: A cut stone water gauge in the falls pool, signed Alder, measures the falls through the seasons.

out_water_gauge.text: Wren copied Alder's water gauge and the island stayed mostly blank.

grove_features.text: In the grove hang a frayed rope ladder into the canopy and stands a small shell-dressed cairn shrine.

out_rotten_ladder.text: A rotten rung broke under Wren; the canopy view was lost.

alder_treetop.text: A plank lookout high in the greatest tree has a brass sighting ring stamped with Alder's name.

out_treetop_view.text: Wren lingered in the treetop and climbed down with a fragment and no chart.

shrine_first_people.text: The cairn shrine, topped with a carved wooden bird, was left by the island's first people.

out_forest_shrine.text: Wren sat before the shrine and only it was set down on the paper.

dell_features.text: The dell has a small spring, a mossy carved bench, a stream running downhill, and a way up to the ridge.

out_dell_doze.text: Wren dozed in the dell and lost the morning.

mapmakers_bench.text: The dell bench is carved with initials, dates and little maps by many mapmakers, Alder among them.

out_carved_bench.text: Wren copied every name on the bench and the island stayed bare.

knotted_rope.text: A knotted rope tied to a root hangs into the sink-hole, left by someone before.

cave_passages.text: Below the sink-hole three passages lead off, of dripping water, glitter, and warm air, and a roof hole of daylight promises a way up.

tide_line_mark.text: A scratched line on the cave wall marks how high the water rises at the turn of the tide.

stream_ways.text: The underground stream runs to a low arch; it can be climbed upward, and a side rift glows with glowworms.

arch_flooding.text: Under the low arch the tide is rising; a dry ledge runs beside it toward a paler light.

out_cavern_flood.text: The tide flooded the arch passage; Wren scrambled back soaked and the caverns stayed a question mark.

spring_underground.text: The underground stream climbs to a sunlit chamber that is the underground face of the island's spring.

quartz_not_treasure.text: The cave glitter is veins of quartz crystal, not treasure.

ochre_handprints.text: Red ochre handprints left long before any mapmaker cover a cave wall.

ochre_map.text: The handprints form a map of the island, marking the spring and the high peak.

out_cave_art.text: Wren copied the ochre map in full and the land above stayed half drawn.

deepglow_cove.text: A glowing passage comes out onto the beach of the hidden cove, and a side branch leads toward lapping water.

deep_glow_seen.text: A glow of light shows ahead in the caves.

bat_colony.text: A colony of bats warms the warm passage.

cave_pup.text: A young seal pup is stranded on a ledge in the bat cave, frightened but unhurt.

pup_sea_tube.text: The cave pup came in through a flooded tube from the sea and was stranded at low tide.

pup_too_heavy.text: Wren cannot lift the seal pup out alone.

out_pup_too_heavy.text: Wren's lone try to coax the pup out failed; Wren marked the sea tube and backed away.

root_vent.text: A root-choked side vent leads out to daylight high on the slope.

skylight_slope.text: A slope of fallen rock climbs toward the skylight hole, and a gallery of stone formations lies to one side.

rock_chimney.text: The last climb to the skylight is a narrow rock chimney.

out_stuck_chimney.text: Wren tired in the chimney and slid back down; the surface stayed out of reach that way.

searcher_lantern.text: Goat bones and a rusted lantern in the gallery show a human searcher came that way before.

out_stone_gallery.text: Wren drew the stone gallery and the island above stayed undrawn.

underground_lake.text: A black underground lake has a raft of old lashed planks on a pale sand beach.

out_lake_dunk.text: A raft lashing snapped and Wren was dunked in the black lake; the crossing failed.

blind_fish.text: Blind white fish drift in the far shallows of the underground lake, and a flowstone stair climbs toward daylight.

out_blind_fish.text: Wren studied the blind fish and the island stayed blank.

stone_footprints.text: Children's footprints turned to stone mark the hidden lake beach.

out_stone_prints.text: Wren mapped every stone footprint and the island stayed nearly blank.

glowworms.text: Thousands of glowworms light the side rift, which pinches to a squeeze one way and holds a still pool the other.

out_stuck_squeeze.text: Wren stuck in the squeeze, wriggled back free, and left the rift as a shaky note.

spring_trickle_heard.text: The glowworm rift slopes toward the trickle of the spring.

out_glowworm_sky.text: Wren lay under the glowworms until the day had moved on.

survey_tower.text: A leaning survey tower built by mapmakers before Wren was born stands on the headland, with a ground room, an outside stair, a cellar hatch, and keeper's quarters.

tower_logbook.text: The tower's ground room holds ruined instruments and a damp swollen logbook recording the tower's last days.

out_tower_log.text: Wren copied Alder's last log entry and carried home a story instead of a map.

alidade.text: Among the ruined instruments a battered brass alidade still works.

stair_gap.text: A span of the outside stair has fallen, leaving a gap; a crumbling ledge offers a slower way around.

out_tower_retreat.text: The crumbling ledge shed stones and Wren retreated; the tower top was never reached.

wren_on_tower_top.text: Wren reached the top of the survey tower.

summit_and_camp_seen.text: The true summit stands higher across the ridge, with a camp tucked below it.

beacon_brazier.text: An old iron beacon brazier stands on a jut of the headland near the tower.

knife_ridge.text: A knife of rock joins the tower to the grassy bench where the camp trail begins.

cellar_stores.text: The tower cellar holds rope, oil, food tins, a lamp, and a leather chart tube.

alder_draft.text: The leather tube holds Alder's half-finished water-stained draft; its note says the good copy went to the ridge camp.

draft_safe_path.text: Alder's draft sketches the safe path up to the ridge.

out_old_draft.text: Wren copied Alder's ruined draft and ended with someone else's map.

wren_has_rope_oil.text: Wren carries rope and a tin of oil from the tower cellar.

chalk_line.text: A chalked surveyor's line by the cellar door points along a marked path to the ridge.

keeper_quarters.text: The keeper's quarters hold a bunk, a cold hearth, a sea chest, and a wall of pinned charts.

wall_charts_other_islands.text: The pinned charts are of a dozen other islands, not this one, all drawn and signed by Alder.

out_chart_wall.text: Wren studied Alder's wall of charts and rowed out with this island blank.

sea_chest.text: The sea chest holds an oilskin coat, a working brass compass, and a child's crayon drawing marked For Alder.

alder_family.text: Alder left a family ashore to go and map the world.

wren_has_compass.text: Wren carries the brass pocket compass from the sea chest.

out_family_drawing.text: Wren sat with the child's drawing and rowed out with the chart bare.

stone_dial.text: A carved stone dial near the beacon gives the bearing to every landmark on the coast.

beacon_needs_fuel.text: The beacon once warned ships off the hidden reef and must have had a fuel store nearby.

fuel_store_found.text: Wren found the beacon's fuel store under a low stone lintel.

fuel_store_not_found.text: Wren searched for the beacon's fuel store and found nothing.

alder_last_note.text: On the fuel store door Alder wrote: Gone to finish the ridge chart, back by the storm.

out_dead_beacon.text: Wren lost an hour at the dead beacon for a plain dead end.

out_keeper_note.text: Wren sat with Alder's last note and the chart stayed empty.

dial_is_alders.text: The stone dial, cut with a name and bearing for every headland, reef and peak, is signed Alder.

out_stone_dial.text: Wren copied every bearing of the stone dial and drew no coastline.

strongbox.text: Under a loose floor slab sits an iron strongbox with a seized lock and a rusted key on a nail.

out_locked_box.text: Wren forced the lock, bent the bar, grazed a knuckle, and the strongbox stayed shut.

strongbox_opened.text: Wren opened the strongbox with the rusted key.

brass_tools_letter.text: The strongbox holds fine brass drawing tools and a sealed letter from Alder to whoever finishes the work.

wren_has_brass_tools.text: Wren carries Alder's brass drawing tools and sealed letter.

alder_letter_text.text: Alder's letter charges the finder to love the island, finish the map, and mind the truth, not the glory.

out_alder_letter.text: Wren read Alder's letter, felt chosen, and went home with the chart undrawn.

flats_tide_rule.text: The Chart House rule of the flats: the sea returns faster than a person can run, so keep one eye on it.

flats_features.text: The flats offer a far sandbar with a wreck, firm channel edges, a strand line of cast-up treasures, and dark mussel beds.

sandbar_wreck.text: A wreck lies out on the distant sandbar.

tide_turning_flats.text: The tide has turned and is sliding back across the flats.

out_flats_cutoff.text: The tide cut Wren off; Wren waded back chest-deep and the flats stayed blank.

flats_sketched.text: Wren sketched the flats and got back to firm ground just ahead of the tide.

valley_stream.text: A green gap in the shore is a valley whose stream climbs toward falling water at its source.

cliff_gap.text: The flats' channels meet at a gap of wet sand into the cliffs, bared only at low water.

strand_bottle.text: On the strand lies a corked bottle with a paper message inside.

alder_bottle.text: The bottle message from Alder says the island is real and its chart waits at the ridge camp for whoever finishes the work.

out_message_bottle.text: Wren kept Alder's bottle note and waited for the ship with a blank chart.

mussel_features.text: Past the mussel beds a seal colony basks on a rock and a deep gully cuts toward the cliffs.

tangled_pup.text: A seal pup on the rock has old fishing net snarled around one flipper.

out_freed_pup.text: Wren freed the netted pup but the colony stampeded and the low-tide window was lost.

gully_weed_lines.text: Weed lines high on the gully walls show how deep and fast it floods.

out_gully_flood.text: Wren dawdled in the gully until the tide came and the shortcut was lost.

great_wreck.text: The great wreck on the bar has a flooded hold, a tilted deck, and a carved figurehead at the bow.

marigold.text: The wreck's bell names her the Marigold, the ship that brought settler families to the island long ago and foundered on the bar.

out_wreck_trap.text: Wren was nearly caught in the flooding hold and got out soaked with the flats unfinished.

out_settler_wreck.text: Wren pieced together the Marigold's story and the flats became a soaking blur.

flats_from_bow.text: From the high bow rail the whole pattern of the flats lies clear.

out_figurehead.text: Wren drew the figurehead and only just made shore ahead of the tide.

dune_marker.text: A weathered surveyor's marker post leans on the highest dune behind the strand.

out_soft_dunes.text: Wren floundered in the soft dunes and gave up the view.

flats_from_dune.text: From the marker dune the whole pattern of the flats opens below.

out_flats_map.text: Wren drew the flats perfectly from the dune and left the rest of the island untouched.

cove_features.text: In the cove a fresh rill trickles down a rock wall, a hand-cut path climbs toward the ridge, and an old compass rose on a rock points up.

out_cove_daydream.text: Wren daydreamed in the calm cove and drew only the cove.

star_slab.text: A rock slab beside the cove path is pecked with dots in a pattern.

star_map.text: The dotted slab is a star map by which the island's first people steered, with a scratch marking the high peak.

out_star_slab.text: Wren copied the star map in full and the coast stayed unfinished.

cove_pools_cave.text: The cove rim holds jewelled tide pools and a low sea cave.

alder_cove_tin.text: In the cove sea cave Alder cut a name and date and left a tin with a spare pencil and a note: The way up is behind you, friend.

out_cove_tin.text: Wren sat with Alder's kind note and climbed out with an empty page.

reef_edge_channel.text: The tide pools map the reef edge and the cove's safe deep channel.

out_reef_pools.text: Wren mapped every tide pool and the island above stayed blank.

spring_five_shores.text: From the spring Wren sees the island's water running five ways to five shores.

out_too_many_streams.text: Wren chased every stream and ended with blue lines and no coast.

drainage_mapped.text: Wren sketched the island's whole drainage from the spring.

high_meadow.text: A high meadow with grazing wild goats lies on the way from the spring to the camp trail, ringed by an old tumbled cairn.

alder_boundary.text: The fallen cairn's capstone carries Alder's survey mark fixing the middle of the island.

out_meadow_nap.text: Wren copied the boundary mark, dozed in the meadow, and went down with half a chart.

camp_interior.text: Alder's camp holds a cot, a cold stove, a tin trunk, and on the table a half-drawn chart.

alder_half_chart.text: Alder's chart shows half the island true, with the high ground and the far shore left blank.

camp_tools.text: Pens, a brass spyglass, and a signal mirror lie set out beside Alder's chart.

finish_note.text: Across the blank, Alder wrote: Finish this, and it is yours, mapmaker to mapmaker.

out_alder_story.text: Wren only copied Alder's half chart; the mate said a copied map is a story, not a survey.

trunk_journal.text: The trunk holds nibs, ink, a cloth for the mirror and spyglass, and Alder's journal.

journal_stops.text: Alder's journal stops mid-sentence the day a storm took the boat that never came back.

alder_journal_story.text: Alder mapped alone for seasons, named the hidden cove, and waited on the ridge for a ship that came too late.

alder_wish.text: Alder's last wish: whoever finds this, finish the chart, and give the island its name.

out_alder_journal.text: Wren read the whole journal and rowed out with a blank chart and Alder's story.

wren_carries_tools.text: Wren carries Alder's tools, the pens and the glass.

summit_cairns_scree.text: Above the camp a line of cairns marks the safe way along a narrow ridge; a bare scree slope offers a shortcut.

out_scree_slide.text: The scree slid under Wren; shaken, Wren judged the summit too far and the high chart stayed unfinished.

ridge_notch.text: The cairns lead through a windy notch to a boulder field below the summit.

summit_view.text: From the summit cairn Wren sees the whole island at once.

out_summit_awe.text: Wren stood gazing from the summit and drew none of it.

out_rushed_muddle.text: Wren rushed every detail and brought down a full chart that was wrong in places.

all_coasts_sighted.text: Wren took careful sightings of every coast from the summit.

reef_cove_fixed.text: Wren fixed the reef, cove and channels for safe landings.

far_shore.text: The wild windward far shore of cliffs, sea stacks and a guarding reef had never been mapped by anyone.

island_fully_surveyed.text: Every part of the island is seen and fixed, ready to draw as one chart with Alder's half.

chart_finished.text: Wren drew the finished chart of the whole island.

chart_unfinished.text: Wren left the island without a finished chart.

banner_blank.text: Alder left the name banner across the top of the half chart empty for whoever finished it.

two_copies.text: Wren drew the chart twice, a master and a working copy.

apprenticeship_won.text: The mate takes Wren on as a Chart House apprentice.

apprenticeship_withheld.text: Wren goes home without the apprenticeship.

out_safe_harbor.text: Wren brought home the safe-landing chart of reef and cove, the map that keeps sailors alive.

out_never_finished.text: Wren kept adding detail until the ship's horn sounded and the map was never done.

island_named_alder.text: Wren named the island Alder's Island.

island_named_both.text: Wren wrote both mapmakers' names on the banner.

out_flawless_survey.text: Wren left the banner blank, signed the survey, and the mate found no fault in it.

out_double_chart.text: Wren presented both charts and won the apprenticeship for judgement.

out_secret_spare.text: Wren gave one chart and quietly kept the spare as the start of a private library.

out_wild_coast.text: Wren brought home a chart of the unmapped windward shore alone, with the rest only sketched.

living_margins.text: Wren ringed the chart's margins with the island's living things.

out_living_chart.text: The mate gave Wren the apprenticeship and the honour of naming the next island.

out_clean_master.text: Wren handed over the clean masterwork and the mate found not one fault.

ship_back_early.text: The ship is already back, a white speck standing off the reef waiting for dusk.

reef_turtle.text: Through the spyglass Wren saw a small turtle tipped on its back in a draining pool out on the reef.

distress_rhythm.text: Flash, pause, flash is the old distress rhythm drilled into every Chart House apprentice.

ship_answers.text: The ship came about and steered for the sheltered cove, answering Wren's signal.

sailors_sent.text: The mate saw the signal and sent two sailors ashore in the boat to the cove.

cove_cave_pup.text: A young seal pup is trapped crying in a sea cave in the cove cliffs, unable to climb out.

out_saved_pup.text: Wren and the sailors lifted the pup out and freed it; the mate called Wren worth keeping.

out_saved_turtle.text: Wren and the sailors carried the reef turtle to deep water; the chart was half finished and the mate offered the place.

n_open.event: Wren is rowed ashore alone at first light with satchel, flask and one blank sheet; the mate sets the test: a true chart by dusk or no apprenticeship.

n_start.event: Five ways lead inland from the beach: mangrove coast, cloud-forest ridge, caverns, survey tower, tidal flats.

mg_enter.event: Wren wades into the mangroves; a log bridge, oyster rocks, a hidden creek and a green lagoon offer bearings.

mg_bridge.event: Halfway across the slippery log Wren spots carved driftwood while the tide rises; a rookery clatters on the far bank.

mg_carve.event: The carving is mapmaker's shorthand with arrows to sea caves and to high ground, a message left on purpose.

mg_readmarks.event: Read the Chart House way, the marks name Alder and promise a chart left at a camp on the ridge.

mg_farbank.event: The rookery bursts up as Wren steps off the log; the path splits between a mud slick and firm palms.

e_mg_mud_trap.event: Wren sinks in the mud slick, and the tide closes over the log bridge and cuts off that corner of coast.

mg_highground.event: Out of the swamp Wren sees the island's northern shape, a reef offshore and a hidden cove; a goat track forks to cove and spring gully.

mg_oyster.event: Among the oyster rocks a small sea turtle lies stranded on its back as the pools drain.

mg_turtle_note.event: The turtle is fine but stuck; Wren weighs righting it now against marking it and signalling the ship later.

e_mg_turtle_seen.event: Wren rights the turtle and it swims free, but the tide returns and only the reef corner gets mapped.

mg_rockpath.event: Past the oyster rocks a cold sweet seep threads inland, sign of a spring on higher ground.

mg_seep.event: The seep climbs into a fern gully; Wren fills the flask; the gully forks to a bright spring pool and a mossy overhang.

mg_overhang.event: Under the overhang lie an old firepit and tin cup, and Alder's name with an arrow uphill toward a camp.

e_mg_shelter.event: Wren sketches the snug shelter, the morning slips by, and only that corner is drawn.

mg_creek.event: The hidden creek runs level under leaves; an otter family slips upstream; trees and a loud heron island offer other ways.

mg_otter.event: Upstream the creek shallows over gravel; the water tastes sweet, so a spring and high ground lie above.

mg_trees.event: Away from the creek, Wren must choose by instinct between a brightness uphill and a level game trail.

mg_gametrail.event: The game trail curls back on itself with no landmark; the bright rise still shows behind.

e_mg_lost.event: The trail returns Wren to the same fallen tree; the wasted hour leaves the coast guessed and its middle blank.

cf_enter.event: The misty cloud-forest slope offers a switchback, a traverse, a hollow with a pale gleam, and a waterfall's roar.

cf_switch.event: On the switchback ledge a bare rock rib and a green shelf both lead up toward the ridge.

cf_ledge.event: The airy rib delivers Wren onto a grassy bench where a worn ridge path climbs higher.

cf_shelf.event: The shelf is a surveyor's contour path that brings Wren to the grassy bench where the ridge path begins.

cf_bench.event: On the windy bench a stony trail climbs toward a grey canvas camp; an ancient grove lies to one side.

cf_campapproach.event: A line of small cairns guides Wren up through broken rock toward the high ridge where the camp must stand.

camp_ascent1.event: On the windy open ridge Wren follows the cairns toward the distant speck of the camp.

camp_ascent2.event: The ridge splits: cairns on a sheltered ledge, an airy crest, or stopping daunted by the height.

e_ascent_daunted.event: Dizzied on the high ridge, Wren edges back and maps it from lower down, leaving the camp out of reach.

camp_ascent3a.event: The sheltered ledge, set with alpine flowers, climbs slowly back to the crest.

camp_ascent3b.event: The airy crest is exhilarating, cloud pouring over, and it comes down to a level shelf of cairns.

camp_ascent4.event: On the level shelf the ways rejoin among clustered cairns; one short pull remains to the camp.

camp_ascent5.event: Against the cliff stands a low camp of canvas and stone with Alder's name painted over the door.

cf_traverse.event: The traverse crosses streams all running downhill; Wren traces one up to the island's spring, with a deer path aside.

cf_upper.event: Higher up, a faint path climbs to the ridge, and the hollow below shows the pale gleam seen that morning.

cf_hollow.event: The gleam is a curtain of white orchids hiding a cleft with a mossy tin box marked with a compass rose.

cf_box.event: The box holds field notes, a pencil stub and a locket with a picture of a girl who looks a little like Wren.

e_cf_locket.event: Wren pockets the locket and climbs on, too distracted by the girl's picture to map more than a scrawl.

cf_notes.event: The notes are Alder's: a chart left at the ridge camp, and a warning that the caverns flood at high tide.

cv_enter.event: Wren climbs down someone's knotted rope into a cavern with passages of dripping water, glitter and warm air, and a skylight hole.

cv_water.event: At an underground stream a scratched tide line warns how high the water rises; the stream offers arch, upflow and a glowworm rift.

cv_arch.event: Under the low arch the tide is rising; a dry ledge runs beside it toward a paler light.

e_cv_flood.event: Past the arch the tide pours in as the scratched line warned; Wren scrambles back soaked and the caves stay a question mark.

cv_upflow.event: Climbing upstream to the spring, Wren reaches a sunlit chamber, the underground face of the island's spring.

cv_glitter.event: The glitter is quartz, not treasure, and among it are ancient red ochre handprints.

cv_ochre.event: The handprints form the oldest map of the island, marking the spring and the high peak, older than the Chart House.

e_cv_paintings.event: Wren copies the ochre map in full; it costs the afternoon, but the keepers' hush says the trade was fair.

cv_deepglow.event: Wren pushes toward the glow and tumbles out into the hidden cove; a side branch murmurs with lapping water.

cv_warm.event: The warm passage holds a bat colony, and below it a seal pup stranded on a ledge far from the sea.

cv_pup.event: The pup came in by a flooded sea tube; Wren cannot lift it alone, but could mark it and signal the ship for help.

e_cv_pup_fail.event: The pup is too heavy and frightened; Wren marks the sea tube for help and backs away.

cv_backout.event: Backing away from the bats, Wren finds a root-choked vent opening on daylight high on the slope.

cv_tohigh.event: Wren climbs out onto the ridge flank, sees the island spread below, and spots a camp on the ridge above.

tw_enter.event: The leaning survey tower, built by mapmakers before Wren's birth, offers a ground room, outside stair, cellar and keeper's quarters.

tw_ground.event: The ground room holds ruined instruments and a swollen logbook of the tower's last days; a floor slab shifts.

e_tw_log.event: The logbook is Alder's; the last entry says the true chart went up to the ridge camp before a storm, and Wren copies it until dusk.

tw_salvage.event: Among the ruins a brass alidade still works; Wren can carry it inland or up the stair first.

tw_toridge.event: With the tower's find stowed, Wren climbs the headland path and sees a camp on the ridge.

tw_stair.event: Two thirds up the outside stair a span has fallen; Wren can stride the gap or try a crumbling ledge.

e_tw_stair_fail.event: The ledge sheds stones and Wren retreats; the tower keeps its view and that corner is drawn from guesswork.

tw_top.event: From the tower top Wren sees ridge, flats, reef and the hidden cove, and a camp below the higher summit.

tw_ridgeway.event: Wren walks a knife of rock from the tower to the grassy bench where the camp trail begins.

tw_cellar.event: The cellar holds rope, oil, food, a lamp and a ribboned leather chart tube.

tw_tube.event: The tube holds Alder's half-finished stained draft; its note says the good copy is at the ridge camp, and it shows the safe path up.

e_tw_draft.event: Wren copies Alder's draft in full and ends the day with another mapmaker's unfinished island and no ground of Wren's own.

tw_supplies.event: Wren takes rope and oil and follows a chalked surveyor's line toward a camp on the ridge.

tf_enter.event: On the mirror-bright flats Wren minds the Chart House tide rule; a wrecked sandbar, firm channels, a strand line and mussel beds beckon.

tf_sandbar.event: The sandbar holds a boat's ribbed hull, but water creeps up from below: the tide has turned.

e_tf_stranded.event: The run is too slow; the tide fills the channels and Wren wades back chest-deep, losing the day to drying out.

tf_sketchrun.event: Wren sketches the wreck fast and reaches firm ground just ahead of the tide; a green gap opens inland.

tf_gap.event: The gap is a valley whose stream climbs toward the sound of falling water at its source.

tf_channel.event: The firm channels gather at a tidal gap into the cliffs; a firm rise leads inland and the great wreck waits on the bar.

tf_cliffgap.event: Wren slips through the low-tide gap in the cliffs into a hidden cove ringed by rock.

tf_strand.event: The strand is heaped with shells, rope, a net float, and a corked bottle with a message inside.

tf_bottle.event: The message is from a mapmaker named Alder: the island is real and its chart waits at the ridge camp for whoever finishes it.

e_tf_bottle.event: Wren keeps Alder's note and waits on the sand for the ship; the apprenticeship must wait for another island.

L_cove.event: The hidden cove is a calm secret pocket with a fresh rill, a hand-cut path to the ridge, and an old compass rose pointing up.

e_cove_rest.event: Wren sits sketching the calm cove, the morning slips away, and only the cove is drawn.

cove_rise.event: A hand-cut path climbs from the low ground past a slab pecked with patterned dots.

cove_starrock.event: The slab is a star map the first people steered by, with a scratch for the high peak, older than the Chart House.

e_star_map.event: Wren copies the star map in full; the coast stays unfinished, but the Chart House keepers fall quiet over it.

cove_ridge.event: The cut path tops out on the windy grassy bench, and a stony trail climbs toward a camp.

L_fresh.event: At the island's spring Wren sees water running five ways to five shores and a camp far up the ridge path.

e_fresh_linger.event: Every stream branches endlessly; by afternoon the map is blue lines with no coast.

fresh_study.event: Wren works out the island's whole drainage from the spring in a clean sketch.

fresh_climb.event: The path climbs onto open ridge and through a high meadow of wild goats toward the camp trail.

fresh_meadow.event: The gentle meadow is ringed by an old tumbled boundary cairn; the camp trail climbs beyond.

fresh_cairn.event: The cairn's capstone carries a survey mark and Alder's name, fixing the middle of the island.

e_fresh_cairn.event: Wren copies Alder's boundary mark, dozes in the warm meadow, and hurries down with half a chart.

L_camp.event: Alder's empty camp holds a cot, a stove, a trunk, and Alder's half-drawn chart with pens, spyglass and signal mirror.

camp_chart.event: Alder's chart is true but unfinished, and across the blank Alder wrote: Finish this, and it is yours.

e_camp_copy.event: Wren copies Alder's half chart; the mate says a copied map is a story, not a survey, and gives no apprenticeship yet.

camp_trunk.event: The trunk holds nibs, ink, a polishing cloth, and Alder's journal, which stops the day a storm took the boat.

camp_journal.event: The journal tells Alder's life on the island, the late ship, and the wish: finish the chart and name the island.

e_camp_journal.event: Wren spends the afternoon on Alder's journal and rows out at dusk with a blank chart and Alder's story.

camp_ready.event: With Alder's tools in hand and half chart under one arm, Wren sets out for the summit.

camp_summitpath.event: Above the camp, carrying Alder's chart and tools, Wren meets a narrow cairned path and a tempting scree shortcut.

e_camp_scree.event: The scree slides out from under Wren; shaken, Wren judges the summit too far and the high chart stays unfinished.

ridge_notch.event: The cairns lead through a wind-funnelling notch to a boulder field below the summit.

wind_gap.event: Wren crosses the boulder field block by block to the bare crown of the island.

L_summit.event: From the summit cairn Wren sees the whole island, with a fierce wind and the light leaning toward afternoon.

e_summit_gaze.event: Wren stares at the vast view until the light turns and reaches the beach with a chart still mostly bare.

summit_survey.event: On Alder's half chart Wren fixes ridge, reef, cove and flats fast, but must choose what to nail down first.

e_ch_rush.event: Wren rushes everything, lines smudge and cross, and the mate calls the full but wrong chart a near miss.

ch_sightings.event: With Alder's spyglass Wren fixes every distant point until the island's bones are pinned true.

ch_reef.event: Wren finishes the reef and cove channels Alder began, the map that keeps sailors alive, with a sliver of light left.

e_ch_reef.event: The mate reads the safe-landing chart, calls it the map that keeps sailors alive, and takes Wren on.

ch_gather.event: In the lee of the cairn Wren lays Alder's chart beside the day's sketches and the whole island fits together.

ch_table.event: With the seeing done, Wren chooses how to draw: bold ink, soft detailed pencil, or two copies.

ch_ink.event: Wren inks the chart with Alder's good pen; the two halves become one finished island.

ch_pencil.event: Wren pencils every detail of the island onto one crowded page as the light nearly goes.

e_ch_dusk.event: Wren keeps adding detail until the ship's horn sounds; the mate says a map never finished is no map at all.

ch_double.event: Wren copies the chart twice, a master for the Chart House and a working copy to keep.

ch_sign.event: Alder left the half chart's name banner blank; Wren must choose a name or sign the survey.

e_ch_alder_name.event: Wren names it Alder's Island; the mate understands the story in the name and takes Wren on.

e_ch_both_name.event: Wren writes both names on the banner; the mate calls it the finest first survey in years and Wren a mapmaker.

e_ch_survey.event: Wren signs the survey small in the corner; the mate finds no fault and offers the apprenticeship on the spot.

ch_sign_double.event: With master and working copy in hand, Wren decides whether to present both or keep the spare.

e_ch_double_win.event: Wren hands over both charts and explains the spare; the mate calls it judgement and takes Wren on.

e_ch_spare.event: Wren gives one fine chart, is welcomed aboard, and quietly keeps the spare as a first private sheet.

summit_signal.event: The ship is already back off the reef; Wren has Alder's mirror and has spied a stranded turtle on the reef.

signal_aim.event: Wren catches the low sun in the mirror and holds a blade of light on the distant sail.

signal_flash.event: Wren flashes the old Chart House distress rhythm through doubt and an aching arm.

ship_turns.event: The ship comes about and steers for the cove, answering the lost mapmaker's mirror; Wren must race down.

race_down.event: Wren runs down cairn to cairn past the camp and the cove path as the ship's boat pulls through the reef.

meet_boat.event: Two sailors land; Wren can lead them to the reef turtle or to a seal pup heard crying in a cove sea cave.

e_rescue_pup.event: Wren and the sailors lift the pup out to the sea; the mate says a mapmaker who saves a life is worth keeping.

e_rescue_turtle.event: Wren and the sailors carry the turtle to deep water; the chart is half finished, and the mate offers the place.

mg_lagoon.event: At the still lagoon lie a half-sunk dugout, a root tunnel, and a driftwood dam.

mg_canoe.event: The dugout is old but sound; Wren must test it carefully or trust it straight into deep water.

e_mg_canoe.event: The dugout leaks and sinks under Wren far from shore; the sketchbook stays dry but the morning is lost.

mg_paddle.event: From the floating dugout the shore traces easily, and a strip of old cleared ground shows across the lagoon.

mg_lagfar.event: On the cleared strip stand a stone mound and posts; a firm path climbs toward the creek.

mg_ruin.event: The mound and posts are a long-abandoned fishing camp, older than the Chart House.

e_mg_village.event: Wren maps the vanished fishing camp stone by stone and goes down at dusk with a village instead of a coastline.

mg_lagtunnel.event: The root tunnel forks: one way brightens toward open sky, the other bores deeper into the dark.

e_mg_tunnellost.event: The tunnel branches endlessly; Wren backtracks by feel and leaves the tangle as a scribble.

mg_dam.event: In the otters' driftwood dam stands Alder's numbered survey stake; the creek runs on inland.

e_mg_stake.event: Wren carries Alder's stake home like treasure and barely lifts the pencil; the map is hardly started.

cf_falls.event: A waterfall pours into a kingfisher pool, with a wet rock scramble, a log above the lip, and pale shapes below.

cf_fallclimb.event: The wet rocks have good holds; Wren can climb carefully to the traverse or scramble up recklessly.

e_cf_slip.event: A mossy hold peels away and Wren slides into the pool, soaked; the sketchbook stays dry but the climbing is over.

cf_fallcross.event: Wren tests and crosses the mossy log above the lip to the upper traverse.

cf_fallpool.event: The pale shapes are a cut stone water gauge signed Alder.

e_cf_gauge.event: Wren copies Alder's water gauge notch by notch, a small marvel, while the island stays mostly blank.

cv_skylight.event: A rock slope climbs toward the skylight hole; a gallery of stone formations glows to one side.

cv_chimney.event: The last stretch is a narrow rock chimney that will go if climbed steadily.

e_cv_chimney.event: Wren rushes the chimney, tires, and slides back down before a slip becomes a fall; another way up must be found.

cv_gallery.event: In the stone gallery lie a fallen goat's bones and a rusted lantern, proof a human searcher came before.

e_cv_lantern.event: Wren draws the frozen stone forest with the lantern in the corner and climbs out with a cave instead of a coastline.

tw_quarters.event: The keeper's quarters hold a bunk, a cold hearth, a latched sea chest and a wall of pinned charts.

tw_wallcharts.event: The charts are of a dozen other islands, all signed Alder: a whole life of mapmaking.

e_tw_charts.event: Wren studies Alder's wall of charts, copies a few, and rows out at dusk with this island blank.

tw_seachest.event: The sea chest holds an oilskin, a working compass, and a child's drawing For Alder from the family left ashore.

e_tw_drawing.event: The drawing undoes Wren; the morning goes to imagining Alder's waiting family, and the chart stays bare.

tf_mussel.event: Beyond the mussel beds seals bask on a rock and a deep gully cuts toward the cliffs.

tf_seals.event: A seal pup is snarled in old net; freeing it may stampede the colony, so Wren could mark it for help instead.

e_tf_seals.event: Wren frees the pup, the colony stampedes, and the low-tide window is lost with the flats half drawn.

tf_gully.event: The gully floor is dry but weed lines far overhead show how deep and fast it floods.

e_tf_gully.event: Wren lingers over the weed lines, forgets the first rule, and splashes out as the tide fills the gully.

ch_farshore.event: Through Alder's glass Wren charts the never-mapped windward shore of cliffs, stacks and reef.

e_ch_farshore.event: The mate whistles at the unknown coast drawn plain; not the masterwork, but new ground, and Wren is kept on.

ch_seal_final.event: The chart is drawn and signed; Wren may ring its margins with the island's living things or hand it over clean.

e_ch_living.event: The mate calls the living chart the island itself on paper and grants the apprenticeship and the naming of the next island.

e_ch_clean.event: The mate checks the clean chart corner to corner, finds no fault, and Wren becomes the House's newest apprentice.

mg_heron.event: Wren poles a reed raft to the loud heron island, with a watching blind, a mud bank and a rookery.

mg_blind.event: The blind was Alder's; its rails carry a tide table and named bearings; a plank walk leads inland toward the seep.

e_mg_tidetable.event: Wren copies Alder's whole carved tide table, then poles back with the island's shape left for another day.

mg_mudbank.event: A firm ribbon of sand crosses the soft mud bank toward a far channel and higher ground.

e_mg_birdstorm.event: The flock explodes up, Wren sinks knee-deep, the tide turns, and the heron island becomes a smudge.

mg_farchannel.event: The ribbon carries Wren to a clear channel and solid ground with a lookout rise beyond.

mg_rookery.event: Wren returns a fallen chick to its branch and sketches the colony; a way leads on to the mud bank.

e_mg_chick.event: Wren watches and draws the herons until the light says how late it is; the coast stays undrawn.

cf_grove.event: The ancient grove holds a frayed rope ladder into the canopy and a small shell-dressed cairn shrine.

cf_canopy.event: The lower rungs hold but the upper ones look rotten; Wren must test each or hurry.

e_cf_ladder.event: A rotten rung breaks; Wren climbs back down shaken and the grove goes on the map as a guess.

cf_treetop.event: A treetop platform has a brass sighting ring stamped Alder; Wren takes sightings over ridge, coast, reef and flats.

e_cf_canopy.event: Wren stays in the treetop until the light changes and climbs down with a lovely fragment and no chart.

cf_shrine.event: The shrine, topped by a carved wooden bird, was left by the island's first people to bless the forest.

e_cf_shrine.event: Wren sits before the shrine, drawing it in the green hush, and carries the stillness home instead of a map.

cv_lake.event: The passage opens on a black underground lake with an old plank raft on a pale sand beach.

cv_raft.event: The raft floats; crossing will work slowly and evenly but haste could snap the lashings.

e_cv_raft.event: A lashing snaps and Wren is dunked in the black lake, hauling raft and dry sketchbook back to the beach.

cv_farcave.event: On the far shore blind white fish drift in the shallows and a flowstone stair climbs to daylight.

e_cv_fish.event: Wren fills pages with the eyeless fish and climbs out with an island still blank.

cv_lakebeach.event: The pale sand holds children's footprints turned to stone, left long before any mapmaker.

e_cv_prints.event: Wren maps every stone footprint and climbs out toward the ridge with the island nearly blank.

tw_beacon.event: Beside the rusted beacon brazier is a carved stone dial giving bearings to every coastal landmark.

tw_brazier.event: The beacon once warned ships off the reef, so a fuel store must be near; searching will cost time.

e_tw_nofuel.event: Wren hunts around the cold brazier, finds no fuel store, and loses an hour to a dead end.

tw_fuelstore.event: In the empty fuel store Alder's last line reads: Gone to finish the ridge chart, back by the storm.

e_tw_note.event: Wren sits with Alder's unanswered message all morning and the chart stays as empty as the store.

tw_viewdial.event: The stone dial, with a name and bearing for every headland, reef and peak, is signed Alder.

e_tw_dial.event: Wren copies every bearing of Alder's dial and draws no coastline between them.

tf_wreck.event: The great wreck on the bar has a flooded hold, a tilted deck, and a carved figurehead.

tf_hold.event: Cargo shows under the hold's water, but the flats have turned silver: the tide is coming back.

e_tf_hold.event: Wren is nearly trapped in the flooding hold, scrambles out soaked, and leaves the flats unfinished.

tf_cargo.event: A green brass bell in the hold names the wreck the Marigold, the ship that brought settlers to the island.

e_tf_bell.event: Wren pieces together the Marigold's ending, a tale to silence the Chart House, while the flats become a soaking blur.

tf_deck.event: From the high bow by the figurehead Wren sees the whole pattern of the flats.

e_tf_figurehead.event: Wren draws the figurehead while the tide cuts the safe way, and makes shore just in time with the coast bare.

cove_pools.event: Jewelled tide pools rim the cove, and a low sea cave breathes with the swell.

cove_seacave.event: In the dry back of the sea cave are Alder's name and a date and a tin with a pencil and a kind note.

e_cove_tin.event: Wren sits undone by Alder's kindness and climbs out with Alder's pencil, a full heart, and an empty page.

cove_rockpool.event: The tide pools map the reef edge and the cove's safe channel, and Wren pencils it in.

e_cove_reefmap.event: Wren maps every pool perfectly, a channel a captain could steer by, and leaves the island above blank.

cv_rift.event: The rift is lit by thousands of glowworms; it pinches to a squeeze one way and holds a still pool the other.

cv_squeeze.event: The squeeze opens into the wider cave; a careful wriggle will pass, a panicky rush will wedge.

e_cv_squeeze.event: Wren sticks fast in the squeeze, breathes out, and wriggles back free, leaving the rift as a shaky note.

cv_glowworm.event: Wren draws the rift by its own light; the ground slopes toward the trickle of the spring.

e_cv_glow.event: Wren lies under the glowworms until the day above has moved on.

cf_dell.event: The hidden dell has a spring, a carved bench, a stream downhill and a way up to the ridge.

e_cf_dell_lost.event: Wren rests on the soft grass, sleeps, and wakes to find the dell has stolen the morning.

cf_dellspring.event: The dell stream gathers to the island's true spring, and Wren sees how the whole watershed fits.

cf_dellcarve.event: The bench is carved with many mapmakers' marks, Alder's name among them.

e_cf_carve.event: Wren copies every name and little map on the bench, and the island itself stays bare.

tw_slab.event: Under the loose slab sits an iron strongbox with a seized lock and a rusted key on a nail.

e_tw_slab.event: The bar bends and grazes Wren's knuckle; the strongbox stays shut.

tw_cache.event: The key turns; the box holds brass drawing tools and a sealed letter from Alder to whoever finishes the work.

e_tw_cache.event: Wren reads Alder's letter of charge and blessing; the reading takes the light and the chart stays undrawn.

tf_dune.event: A surveyor's marker post leans on the highest dune, but the soft sand is exhausting and the tide will not wait.

e_tf_dune.event: The dune slides away under every step; Wren gives up the crest and the flats go down as a scribble.

tf_marker.event: From the marker dune the whole flats lie below like a chart, and Wren sketches fast.

e_tf_marker.event: Wren perfects the flats from the dune again and again; the rest of the island lies untouched.
